hero.title: Picksell
hero.description: EU marketplace and payment system powered by open banking technology

meta.role: Led the design team, art direction, product strategy, core concepts and identity
meta.scope: Discovery → Brand Guidelines → App MVP → Merchant platform MVP →  Launch  + Support
meta.team: Up to 6 designers: product and graphic

parts.label: Identity
parts.text: Unclear flows needed a friendlier voice, so I created a pixel mascot that helps people from login through placing an order, then led the illustrations and animations that carried that voice through the product.

parts.label: Customer app
parts.text: The React Native MVP made payments from external shops simple, with KYC that felt as easy as a normal checkout. The architecture was designed so the product could grow into a full marketplace.

parts.label: Web
parts.text: The merchant platform could work as a payment method or as the shop itself. We started with existing shops — products, billing, and a to-do onboarding — so they could go live while heavier catalog flows were still in progress.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: Open Banking and KYC flows varied significantly across banks. API responses were unpredictable, and some banks redirected users to external apps or websites.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: I analyzed regulatory requirements, bank documentation, API responses, and possible fallback scenarios.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We designed a flexible interface framework that could adapt to anything from a single input to 20+ fields and handle external redirects consistently.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A scalable KYC and payment flow that made Open Banking feel as simple and familiar as adding a card.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: The MVP focused on payments, but the product needed to evolve into a full-cycle marketplace without a major redesign.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We mapped the future customer journey, marketplace features, and dependencies between payments, products, orders, and merchant tools.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We designed the navigation and product architecture to support both the initial payment-focused MVP and future online shopping scenarios.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A scalable foundation that allowed Picksell to launch quickly and expand into a marketplace as the product gained traction.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: Traditional merchant tools often force sellers to create separate, disconnected product entries for every size, color, or variation.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We analyzed common catalog-management patterns and the difficulties merchants faced when updating large numbers of duplicated products.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: I designed a component-based product editor where one master product contained all its variants, while still supporting CSV imports.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A single source of truth that made catalogs faster to create, easier to maintain, and less prone to inconsistencies.

beats.label: Problem
beats.text: Six designers were working across three platforms and more than 1,000 screens, creating a high risk of inconsistency and duplicated work.

beats.label: Research
beats.text: We audited shared patterns, platform-specific requirements, accessibility standards, and technical constraints.

beats.label: Iterations
beats.text: We built shared components, page-level templates, dedicated libraries, and a unified illustration and motion system.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.text: A single source of truth across all platforms, including 1,500+ design elements and 150+ illustrations and animations, fully aligned with WCAG standards.
